rule: Approval-engine statuses are INTERNAL. They are surfaced on approval screens (SCR-03, SCR-29) only, and are mapped to a C3 business status on the underlying object. An approval status must NEVER be rendered on a business screen as if it were a C3 status. A contract test enforces this.
relationship_to_C3: Label-overlapping but NAMESPACE-disjoint. Four codes share a label with a C3 business status - APPROVED, REJECTED, RETURNED and EXCEPTION_PENDING - and that overlap is deliberate and reviewed, not accidental. They are NOT the same fact: an approval instance being APPROVED is a decision on one object version, whereas a purchase order being APPROVED is a document lifecycle state. They must never be the same identifier in code, and the engine maps one to the other explicitly via maps_to_business_status. tests/test_contracts.py asserts the overlap is EXACTLY these four, so a fifth accidental collision fails the build.

instance.description: Lifecycle of one approval instance over one object version.

statuses.meaning: At least one stage is PENDING. The object cannot proceed.
Every applying stage met quorum. Downstream action permitted.
A stage rejected. Terminal for this object version; a new version may be raised.
Sent back to the requestor for correction.
Withdrawn by the maker before a decision.
The object's content hash changed under an open instance. Auto-superseded; never a silent approval.
Routing could not complete - no independent approver, or no matching rule. FAILS CLOSED. Requires administrator intervention.

stage.description: Lifecycle of one stage instance within an approval instance.

statuses.meaning: The stage's applies_when predicate evaluated false. RECORDED, NEVER OMITTED - an auditor must be able to see what did not run, and why.
SLA breached; assignment extended to the escalation target. The original assignees remain PENDING.

assignment.description: State of one approver's assignment to one stage instance.

statuses.meaning: An approval_action row exists for this assignee on this stage.
Assignment removed - role revoked, delegation expired, or stage closed by quorum before this assignee acted.

invariants: An instance in EXCEPTION_PENDING has never auto-approved and never will. An unroutable object is a configuration defect, not an approval.
A SKIPPED stage always carries a skip_reason and is always visible in the approval timeline.
An ESCALATED stage does not remove the original assignees - escalation adds capacity, it never removes accountability.
approval_action rows are append-only and hash-chained on stream approval:{instance_id}. No status transition may rewrite history.
